findings.claim: The comparator can return a non-zero value when `a` and `b` are the same wildcard string, violating the `compare(x, x) === 0` contract.
findings.rationale: With the new expression, `compareKey('.*', '.*')` returns 1 and `compareKey(TAIL, TAIL)` returns -1 instead of 0. In practice the inputs are usually distinct object keys so this may never be hit, but an inconsistent comparator can yield implementation-defined ordering in `Array.prototype.sort` and makes the function unsafe for any future caller that can pass equal keys. Cheap to fix with an explicit `a === b ? 0 : ...` guard. Medium confidence it is currently unreachable, hence low severity.

findings.claim: Only the `a`-side branch was updated; the `b`-side branch still returns a constant, so the antisymmetry of the new wildcard ordering is accidental rather than explicit.
findings.rationale: `compareKey(TAIL, ONLY)` falls into the first branch and returns 1, while `compareKey(ONLY, TAIL)` returns -1, which happens to be consistent. But the `else if` here is never reached when `a` is a wildcard, so the rule 'ONLY precedes TAIL' lives in exactly one place with no mirrored logic; reordering these branches later would silently break antisymmetry. Moderate confidence this is a robustness concern rather than a live bug.

findings.claim: Swapping the relative order of `.*` and the tail wildcard changes regex alternation priority and may make tail-wildcard routes unreachable.
findings.rationale: These sorted keys are joined into a regular expression alternation, where the first matching alternative wins. `.*` matches every remaining input (including the empty string), so placing it before the tail wildcard means the tail-wildcard alternative can never be reached for any input the only-wildcard node also accepts. Previously both wildcards were pushed to the end by an (inconsistent) comparator; now the order deterministically favors `.*`. This can change which handler wins for paths matched by both wildcard kinds. Not fully certain of the intended precedence since it depends on how the node tree builds the alternation, but a test covering a path matched by both wildcards is warranted.
